stem: Which one of the following statements about infectious mononucleosis (glandular fever) caused by Epstein–Barr virus is correct?

options.text: It can result in grey-yellow exudative tonsillitis that can be indistinguishable from bacterial infections
It is associated with high fever, malaise, generalized tender lymphadenopathy and hepatosplenomegaly
It is only spread via kissing
It can be identified using Monospot or EBV-specific serology

explanation: Infectious mononucleosis is commonly diagnosed with heterophile antibody testing (Monospot) or EBV-specific serology. The other options include true clinical features or incorrect statements about transmission and treatment, but only one best answer is requested.
rationale: The original item had multiple correct answers, so it was rewritten into a single-best-answer question focusing on diagnosis, which has one clearly best option.

optionExplanations.A: This is true, but it is a clinical feature rather than the best single answer in this revised item.
optionExplanations.B: This is also true; however, only one best answer is required.
optionExplanations.C: False. EBV is not spread only by kissing; saliva is common, but other routes and close contact can occur.
optionExplanations.D: False. Amoxicillin is not a treatment for EBV and may precipitate a rash.
optionExplanations.E: Correct. Monospot and EBV-specific serology are used to support the diagnosis.
